next_question: Change the level of description a fifth time and change what is being bounded: stop asking WHETHER an inherited mechanism can transfer to an unseen site, and measure THE SIZE OF THE SURFACE OVER WHICH INHERITANCE COULD POSSIBLY AMORTIZE. This packet's deepest result is not about a key or a cache. It is that on the credential-free public HTTP substrate SPIDER can actually observe without credentials, there is very little that only a prior episode can know: the five reachable real sites exposed 0.000 session-scoped identifiers, offered no write verb, and the only identifiers they expose are the sites own public resource ids, which a fresh episode re-reads for about 119 tokens per observation against the audited 763.06-token per-observation floor from EXP-INTEL-36287179392. All 48 C-CROSSSITE events in the Codex and every frontier inheritance packet measured whether a mechanism TRANSFERS; none measured whether there is anything to transfer, and the one measurement attempted here failed on instrument validity rather than returning an answer. The concrete falsifiable question: on real credential-free sites that do have action-gating structure rather than five always-200 JSON endpoints, what FRACTION of action-gating objects is reachable by a single unconditional GET from a root observation and therefore free to re-derive at the established observation floor, versus requires a discovered path and therefore costs cross-episode state, and does that fraction move the sign of the amortization comparison? Preregister with no new infrastructure, stdlib HTTP only, no browser, no docker, no model key: (i) a RE_DERIVABLE arm that discards all prior state and re-reads the root each episode, carrying the audited 763-token structural representation so observation cost is not silently discarded; (ii) a CACHE_AND_REVALIDATE arm that binds a stable, agent-visible identifier of the gating object and must re-fetch it before replay, charged honestly; (iii) a MANDATORY null arm on a substrate where the only readable identifier is session-scoped or the only reachable path is discovered, which must produce a measurable wrong action or a measurable cost gap, and which MAY be preregistered in advance as a COST null instead of a WRONGNESS null if no credential-free site with CSRF or a write surface is reachable, so the null arm is never again vacuous on this substrate class; and (iv) a mandatory RE_VALIDATE arm that pays the re-fetch price, so break-even is measured rather than assumed. FOUR PRE-FREEZE GATES, each a repair of a specific failure in this packet and none optional. (1) A primary endpoint whose ground truth is INDEPENDENT OF HTTP STATUS: a preregistered declared plan action per span, verified independently of any arm, reusing the parent packet CTRL-SHARED-GROUND-TRUTH pattern, because this packet set correct = response_code == 200 in every arm (research/frontier/realweb_arms.py:311, 369, 428, 495), which made span_level_action_correctness identically 1.0000 for all five executable arms, gave the primary endpoint zero dynamic range, and left the frozen clause INHERITED > COLD + 0.05 arithmetically unsatisfiable at greater than 1.05. (2) A pre-freeze satisfiability audit of EVERY threshold against the measured baseline range, and in particular no clause of the form treatment > baseline + delta without a preregistered baseline_max <= 1 - delta, because a saturating baseline made the frozen success rule unfireable regardless of the mechanism under test. (4) ONE declared cost basis on a BODY-SENSITIVE observation representation, with a stated token-to-latency and token-to-dollar mapping or an explicit statement that UNKNOWN is the honest product answer, because MinimalObservation.to_tokens() (realweb_substrate.py:101-115) omits the response body and therefore cannot distinguish re-derivation from replay on JSON APIs. why_next: This packet attempted the identifier-availability axis that the parent handoff proposed, and it failed on instrument validity rather than returning an answer, so the axis is not resolved in either direction and simply repeating it would be a rename. But the failure is itself informative, and it points somewhere else. What the run actually demonstrated is that on the credential-free public HTTP substrate SPIDER can observe without credentials, there is very little cross-episode state worth having: the five reachable sites exposed 0.000 session-scoped identifiers, no write verb was available, and the only identifiers present were the sites own public resource ids, which any fresh episode re-reads for about 119 tokens per observation. Every experiment in the inheritance thread has asked whether a mechanism TRANSFERS to an unseen site. None has asked whether there is anything that only a prior episode could know, which is the question that decides whether transfer is worth anything at all. Three further facts make that reframe the right move rather than a consolation prize. First, the two inheritance questions the program keeps re-asking, whether a sound cross-episode cache exists and what the minimum agent-visible persistent state is, are both blocked upstream of any measurement frontier can perform: the committed kernel cannot execute an inherited mechanism, so no treatment arm can be built until product lands one, and this Director confirmed that directly in src/spider/kernel.py. Second, the real-Web substrate premise is now discharged, so a properly designed measurement on real sites is cheaper than it has ever been, and the mandate's own directive, to prefer the cheapest sufficient substrate until a question genuinely requires a more expensive one, points the same way. Third, the re-derivable-surface question is decidable with a null control and a positive control that can both actually fire, which the questions just attempted demonstrably cannot: the null arm here had no wrong action available and the primary endpoint had no dynamic range. The proposed question is therefore orthogonal in level of description, not in wording: from whether a cache key is sound, to how large the surface is that a cache could amortize over. If the re-derivable fraction is high, C-CROSSSITE is not unsound but superfluous at any cache design, which is a decisive architectural fact at a different level and a far stronger statement than a prevalence estimate. If it is low, inheritance has a real surface and the sound-cache question becomes worth its cost again. Both branches decide something, which the identifier-availability axis as frozen could not.

recommended_action: Do not chain another Frontier packet on identifier availability, and do not repair, re-run or re-freeze this instrument. This packet bought two things and lost the measurement. It bought a substrate: credential-free real websites are reachable, executable and cheap from this repository with stdlib HTTP alone, and that capability is now proven and should be reused. It bought a hard dependency with an exact location: the committed kernel at src/spider/kernel.py cannot turn an observation into an EXECUTABLE inherited mechanism, so the treatment arm here was untestable and C-CROSSSITE, C-PARAM-INHERIT, C-LLM-INHERIT and C-PRODUCT-ECON are all blocked on product landing that capability. It lost the measurement, and it lost it in a way worth stating plainly: the frozen primary endpoint had no declared ground truth and was evaluated by an HTTP-200 predicate, which made it 1.0000 for every arm that could issue a request, which in turn made the frozen success clause INHERITED greater than COLD plus 0.05 arithmetically unsatisfiable at greater than 1.05 for any mechanism at all. The precondition estimate is a ratio of distinct identifier keys to episodes rather than a fraction of spans, over six classified items on five sites, and it flips from 0.060 to 0.50 with the denominator. The null control had no wrong action available and the prereg's own mitigation for that risk was not implemented. The treatment arm was a stub that charged nothing to the ledger, so its cost of 0.0 is a non-execution artifact rather than amortization. The cost ledger omits the response body, so it cannot distinguish re-derivation from replay on JSON APIs. And no durable raw evidence exists for any of it. Record four things as this lane's durable contribution. (1) C-CROSSSITE is held at HYPOTHESIS with no evidence in either direction: the precondition is unevaluable, the transfer was never exercised, and the registry next_gate, a true website holdout without site identity leakage, is untouched because no distillation ran and no TRAIN site was contacted. (2) A fourth, and the cleanest, instance of the program-level instrument failure class the Global Director named, and the first one DESIGNED IN rather than inherited: a frozen success rule that no mechanism could satisfy, an endpoint whose ground truth is a server response code, an estimator whose numerator and denominator are different units, and a cost ledger blind to the quantity it prices. Transmit these to C-MEAS-VALID in physics and runtime by exact reference, and treat the pre-freeze satisfiability audit this cycle already mandated as the control that would have caught all four. (3) The reusable instrument lesson from the parent packet was violated silently and that is itself the finding: an endpoint whose ground truth is the server's own response code cannot separate a mechanism from no mechanism, so a declared plan action verified independently of any arm, the parent's CTRL-SHARED-GROUND-TRUTH pattern, is a precondition and not a nicety. (4) The honest economic statement is UNKNOWN: on credential-free public HTTP there is very little that only a prior episode can know, the sites expose no session-scoped identifiers and no write verb, and their identifiers are public constants any episode re-reads cheaply, which is a reason to suspect the amortizable surface is small but is not yet a measurement of it. Then take next_question to the Global Research Director pulse as this lane's proposal and not as an authorization: measure the size of the surface over which inheritance could possibly amortize, the fraction of real action-gating objects reachable by a single unconditional GET from a root observation, rather than asking a sixth time whether a mechanism transfers. That question is orthogonal in level of description, it reuses the substrate this packet proved, it needs no absent capability to be asked, and both of its branches decide something, which the axis just attempted could not. If the Director instead redirects Frontier, the two facts worth carrying intact to whichever lane takes them are the committed-kernel blocker with its exact file and line, and the body's absence from the observation representation, because between them they explain why this program has never been able to price inheritance honestly on anything resembling its target domain. And C-CROSSSITE should not be advanced, downgraded or closed by anyone until a primary endpoint with a real ground truth and an estimator with matching units exist.
